title: yencoding serde feature is optional but mime-tree always enables serde unconditionally
description: yencoding/Cargo.toml declares serde as an optional feature (`#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(Serialize, Deserialize))]` on YencMetadata and DecodedPart). However, mime-tree/Cargo.toml depends on yencoding without specifying the serde feature, and mime-tree itself always derives Serialize/Deserialize on its own types. If mime-tree uses YencMetadata or DecodedPart in its own Serialize/Deserialize impls or re-exports them through InlineYEncBlock, there is a hidden dependency: mime-tree's serde impls will silently work only if yencoding's serde feature happens to be enabled (it isn't in mime-tree's dep spec). What goes wrong: a downstream user of mime-tree who tries to serialize an InlineYEncBlock will get a compile error because YencMetadata lacks Serialize unless they also explicitly enable yencoding/serde in their own Cargo.toml — an invisible transitive requirement. Fix: mime-tree should either enable serde on its yencoding dep, or stop embedding YencMetadata/DecodedPart in its own serializable public types. Files: mime-tree/Cargo.toml, yencoding/Cargo.toml, mime-tree/src/yenc.rs.
close_reason: mime-tree unconditionally depends on serde (workspace invariant). yencoding's serde is optional because standalone yEncoding users don't need it. When mime-tree depends on yencoding, it doesn't need yencoding's serde feature — mime-tree does its own serialization of its own types.
